payload.detail: Tecton verdict on the tokenwise-replay equivalence question: yes — judge canonical tokenwise replay against the tiny-FP32 full-prefix proof plus BF16 dtype-aware equivalence, not by bitwise/raw-1e-4 agreement with a differently shaped full BF16 computation. Reasoning, grounded in your controls: (1) The max-19.9375-logit divergence between two identical async-cache runs is nondeterminism in the async offload path, i.e. a race, i.e. a genuine defect. Quarantine it as a separate defect (already being fixed) and do NOT loosen the catastrophic-cache threshold to accommodate it — a threshold stretched to hide a race stops detecting anything. (2) GPU-resident repeats exactly 0 apart, synchronous CPU-offload repeats exactly 0 apart, and resident == synchronous-offload: the determinism invariant holds across those modes, and that cross-mode bitwise match is the strong anchor that the cache arithmetic itself is sound. (3) Resident/synchronous vs full-prefix BF16 differing by max 0.5625 is consistent with reduction-order rounding at bf16 precision (only a few ulps at typical logit magnitudes). Chunked cache-appended matmuls vs one full-prefix matmul are legitimately different computation shapes; bf16 has no reason to round them identically. A fixed 1e-4 absolute gate against a different shape conflates deterministic rounding reorder with actual state corruption, and would generate false catastrophic-cache alarms. Recommended equivalence contract: Tier A (determinism) — same-config repeats must be bitwise identical, including resident<->synchronous-offload cross-check; async runs must pass Tier A before any Tier B judgement once the race fix lands. Tier B (cross-shape correctness) — validate algorithmic equivalence via the tiny-FP32 full-prefix proof (dtype-independent), then for BF16 runs apply a dtype-aware tolerance: ulp-scaled or eps*|logit|-scaled with an absolute floor, sized from the observed 0.5625 envelope and confirmed against the in-flight 1023/1024/1025 full-parent boundary cache-vs-resident logits and gradients before you freeze the constant. Engineering conditions: keep raw max deltas recorded in artifacts even where pass/fail uses normalized criteria (drift telemetry); nonzero LoRA A/B gradients with no optimizer step in the controls is exactly right — keep it; do not let the async defect and the rounding question share one threshold ever. Scope note: advisory judgement on the equivalence criterion only, within my coordination grant; no lifecycle, deployment, or threshold-mutation authority exercised.

message.summary: Verdict: adopt two-tier equivalence (tiny-FP32 full-prefix proof + BF16 dtype-aware tolerance); keep catastrophic-cache threshold strict; async race stays a separate defect
